meta.title: A third, higher own bid leaves the leader unchanged
gaps: The setup already has both QA vendors bid, and no supported operation clearly creates a third own bid for a vendor that has already bid.
The available vocabulary does not expose the existing bid prices, so the new bid cannot be guaranteed to be higher than both existing bids.
The comparison read-back does not expose an explicit L1 label; the plan checks that QA vendor 1 remains the best bidder and QA vendor 2 is not a best bidder.

words.preconditions: A fresh published RFQ event with two QA vendors invited, each with a submitted bid; bidding still open.
steps: A second QA vendor opens a bid on the pricing round.
A second QA vendor prices the line on the bid.
A second QA vendor submits the bid.

As the buyer, read the round's comparison (ranks, best bidder) and check that “auction identifiers data › QA vendor 1 › inline › the line › rank › best bidder” equals true; “auction identifiers data › QA vendor 2 › inline › the line › rank › best bidder” is not true.
words.expected: The app accepts it. Read back afterwards: “auction identifiers data › QA vendor 1 › inline › the line › rank › best bidder” equals true; “auction identifiers data › QA vendor 2 › inline › the line › rank › best bidder” is not true.
